summary: Agent inbox puts every agent run in one list, grouped by what it needs from you: Needs you, Running and Done. A run waiting for you has Approve, a failed one has Retry, and the running ones have live clocks. When a run changes group it glides to its new place, so you can follow it.
use: When several agents run at once and people need one place to see which ones are waiting for them.
When some runs need a person's approval before they go on, like publishing a page.
When a run can fail for a reason that a retry fixes, like a rate limit, and people should retry it from the list.
When people want to see what finished recently, and when.
features: `runs` is the list. Each run has a `title`, the `agent` running it, a `group` of `needs`, `running` or `done`, and a `detail` line, like "Waiting for your approval" or "Editing frame 3 of 6".
Each group shows its count, or a quiet line when it's empty, like "Nothing needs you". The line beside the title reads "2 need you", or "All clear · 4 done today".
`onApprove` adds a filled Approve button to the runs that need you. A run with `failed` turns red and gets a white Retry button instead, through `onRetry`; `why` adds a tooltip on its detail line.
A running run spins and its clock counts on from its `seconds`. A finished one shows a green check, when it `ended`, and its agent.
Each row starts with the agent's first letter on its `color`.
When a run moves to another group, every row and group title glides to its new place and the moving row rides above the rest.
a11y: Each group is a labelled `section`, and its runs form a list.
Approve and Retry are buttons named for their run, like "Approve Publish the pricing page".
The line beside the title is announced politely when it changes.
With reduced motion the rows move without gliding.

faq.a: No. It calls `onApprove` with the run's id. Start the run in your own code and move it to `running`, then to `done` when it ends.

faq.q: Where does a moved run go in its group?
faq.a: Wherever it sits in `runs`. The demo puts a moved run first, so the latest change is at the top.

faq.q: Do the clocks need updating every second?
faq.a: No. Pass the `seconds` a run has been going and its clock counts on by itself. Pass a new value and it counts on from that.

faq.q: Can I name the groups differently?
faq.a: Not yet. The groups are Needs you, Running and Done; `title` and `status` change the header.
